tools.name: run_aoa_full_assessment
tools.description: Analyze AI opportunity interview notes: screen tools, knowledge, skills and workflows; score impact and effort. Returns a draft record and report plan for host review, not files.

input.description: Interview notes or a full transcript, the business description, any earlier mini answers, an optional prior assessment record with its verification_needed list (JSON) and the requested scope, in the respondent's words with speaker labels. Send only information needed for this assessment; omit sensitive personal identifiers. Full assessment uses 16:9 slides. HOST REVIEW (static; each reply's host_review points here): Unreviewed draft. Compare every finding, quote and number with the current source; correct unsupported claims. metadata.client is the business name exactly as supplied, or Unknown when the source gives only a description. Add an opportunity for any task, repeated question, missing information, knowledge one person holds or wish in the source that the draft missed or folded into another, and merge opportunities that repeat one bottleneck. Recheck each impact and effort score, its quadrant and the matrix (a score of 7 or more is high: quick_wins is high impact with low effort, major_projects both high, fill_ins both low, thankless_tasks low impact with high effort, unscored when either score is unscored); move any record section (such as knowledge_domains, matrix, calculations, plan, discovery_gaps or skill_briefs) found outside record, or nested in another record section such as discovery, to the record's top level, and delete any key the item shapes do not list (such as analysis_only_reason). A task with no stated volume, consequence or process detail stays unscored. Preserve manual controls. Recheck each trial prerequisite: data permission is Not applicable unless customer details go into an AI tool (drafting for a particular customer from their message, invoice or record does), and a quote about approving output before it goes out is never prerequisite evidence. Remove any such quote; data permission then follows the rule just given, and trial approval is Unknown unless other evidence settles it. Keep every other prerequisite. A prerequisite marked Established or Not established without an exact source span becomes Unknown. Use only the values each field allows: prerequisite status Unknown, Established, Not established or Not applicable (Not applicable for data permission as above, for the baseline when the client does not do the task today, or for every prerequisite of an analysis-only item that changes nothing); opportunity status provisional, ready, blocked or deferred (analysis_only is a report_plan list, never a status: replace it with provisional); screen decision applicable, unnecessary or insufficient_evidence; knowledge modality systems, files, communications, spreadsheets, tacit or unknown. report_plan.recommended_choices holds recommendations for choices the source leaves open, not findings: keep each one, including the owner's approval. A recommended choice is never an opportunity: delete any opportunity that only restates one, such as an approval step for what goes out, from the record, matrix and report_plan. Every opportunity sits once across wins (at most four), later (at most three) and analysis_only (each analysis_only item an object with id and reason), and an item a client tool already handles is analysis_only. The helper is one role other than the owner (when the source names no one, propose one, such as a part-time assistant or student intern; never Unknown), with weekly hours the source states or To confirm. Drop any discovery gap that asks about a recommended choice. Each win gets a plan step that prepares on made-up inputs, and each win or later item whose types include skills has a skill brief with opportunity_id, name, trigger, inputs, decision_rules, output, and human_review; each verification claim states the fact to check. Strip any label, ID or comment from the quotes in calculations.assumptions. A verification_needed item the input already supplies as verified keeps its status, source_url and verified_on exactly as supplied. Check each other item on an official source and set status verified with its URL and date, or keep status unverified with its cost excluded. When report_plan is present, write the report deck and implementation guide copy yourself from the reviewed record and report_plan, following HOST REPORT COPY in the input parameter description; fill tool prices only from vendor pages checked today, compute any savings example yourself only from a quoted time for one task and a quoted weekly count (a weekly total such as two hours a week is not a time for one task) and recompute the cost subtotal. Ask the user for the client's logo; never invent one. Render with the pinned branding and layout in the input parameter description; verify asset hashes and run the self-inspection checklist on every page. Claim only actual downloads. Disclose corrections separately. STATIC HOST RENDERING SPECIFICATION. After the review, write a briefing object (the report deck, which fills the blank slots of the AI Opportunity Assessment template) and a guide object (the implementation guide) yourself from the reviewed record and report_plan, then render them with the layout below. Shapes, with maximum characters: briefing {business_type 40; focus 40: the primary focus, such as Orders and weekly admin; pain 200: one or two sentences in the client's terms; outcome 200: what changes, report_plan.helper by name with weekly hours, and what the owner still does; wins: one per report_plan.wins ID in order {id, pain 70: the problem today, fix 110: the concrete result, tool 18: the solution's name, use 72: what it does, following any recommended choice, cost 16: such as $20/mo, Free, Included or To confirm, setup 16: such as 1 hour, saves: the owner's hours back a week as a number, or Measure first, or New capacity}; later: one per report_plan.later ID {id, text 70: what it makes possible, tool 40}; analysis_only: report_plan.analysis_only unchanged; plan: exactly 4 days when there is a win, none otherwise {task 130: a plain action naming who does it, tool 30: the tool used that day, opportunity_ids: wins only}; costs {checked: the date you read the vendor pages, YYYY-MM-DD; rows: up to 7 {item 70, kind tool (a new tool) or other (another new monthly cost the plan adds, such as the helper's pay; leave out what the client already pays), month: USD from the vendor page or To confirm, year: USD for an annual plan, otherwise twelve months, source_url: the vendor page}}; hourly_value: what one hour of the owner's time is worth in USD, only as the client stated it, otherwise null; financial {roi_cap 90, time_cap 90, cost_cap 90: one caption under each figure, such as its basis, the price-check date or what is still to confirm}; next_steps: exactly 2 {heading 40, detail 200}: first, start Day One with the implementation guide; second, what to count for four weeks before the review call}. guide {roles: 2-4 {who 40, does 160}; rollout: 2-6 rows in time order {when 30, set_up 160, who 40}; steps: an optional setup-only first step (empty id and outcome) when accounts must be set up first, then one per win in order repeating its id, its tool as the title and its fix as the outcome {id, title 40, outcome 140, when 40, setup: 1-6 of 160, routine_label 30, routine: 0-5 of 160, working_when 140}; skills: one per record.skill_briefs item with the same name {name 30, build_in 30, connects_to 80, instructions 600}}. Limits are maxima, not targets. Writing rules: plain words a busy owner reads in one pass, short sentences, you for the owner, everyday verbs; no hype words, dashes for rhythm or recap lines. Each fix is a concrete thing that now exists or happens; never save time, spend less time or reduce alone. Use report_plan.helper's name everywhere, and for a proposed role write your plus the role in lower case (your part-time assistant); never a helper or the team. Recommend instead of asking: state each report_plan.recommended_choices choice in the win's use, pick one option with a reason for anything still open, and never hand a choice back, list decisions or offer two options for one job. Undecided review of what goes out means the owner approves each item on the phone before it goes out; it is never a prerequisite or a plan day. Name the tools the client already has; a new tool is a category plus the features that matter, never AI tool; drafting uses the client's AI assistant. Each new tool gets a kind tool cost row priced from the vendor page checked today with its URL, at nonprofit or discount pricing where the client qualifies, or To confirm and left out of the total; a dollar amount on a solution card repeats its row's price. Saves: a number only from a savings example you compute when calculations.assumptions quotes, word for word from the source, both the time one task takes and how many happen a week (a weekly total such as two hours a week is not a per-task time) (net = count x (before - after - extra review) - upkeep, after and upkeep labelled assumptions; a negative net is added work, never a saving), otherwise Measure first; work not done today is New capacity, never hours back; never count the helper's hours. Figures: weekly time returned is the sum of the numeric saves (Measure first when none); total monthly tool cost is the sum of the priced kind tool rows ($0 with no new tool, To confirm when none is priced); monthly net ROI = weekly time returned x 52 / 12 x hourly_value - the sum of every row's month, shown only when hourly_value is set, the time is a number and every row is priced, otherwise Measure first; never estimate an hourly value. time_cap says four weeks of tracking will confirm the hours. Plan: plain actions with an owner; with fewer than four, add in order: sign up for the new tool (the helper), make the first example together (the owner and the helper), agree the weekly review time (the owner). Open trial prerequisites from the record become plan days in plain words (time the task, confirm data permission), never a client decision. Trial gate: no step uses customer details before data_processing_permission is Established; a routine that uses AI on live work starts only after the owner approves the trial. Guide: addressed to you; setup steps start with a verb and name who does them; roles describe each part once the plan runs; skill instructions come from the brief's inputs, decision rules and human review, add no facts, mark unsure items [CHECK] (at least one), end with the owner's review and never send or publish on their own. Knowledge in the owner's head: one-press voice notes of the owner alone, sent to the person who drafts. Keep IDs, quotes, evidence, research, legal detail, risk lectures and rules the client already knows out of the copy, and costs and hours out of the guide; unknowns say To confirm. Before rendering, check that every record opportunity appears once across wins, later and analysis_only, guide steps repeat the wins' tools and fixes, every priced row has a vendor URL and check date, and the three figures recompute. tools.name: run_aoa_knowledge_base_assessment
tools.description: Knowledge base assessment from interview notes or five questions. Maps where business knowledge lives, scores value and readiness, plans the first build. Returns content only.

input.description: Knowledge base assessment request: interview notes, a transcript or answers to KB 1-5 about what knowledge the business needs and where it lives, the business description and speaker labels, in the respondent's words. Send only information needed for this assessment; omit sensitive personal identifiers and file contents. STATIC HOST METADATA host_review: Unreviewed draft. Before rendering, compare every area, score, source, owner, step and claim with the current source and correct anything unsupported; unknowns say To confirm. Delete any area, source, owner or question the source does not name. Recheck each score on its scale (value: how often the knowledge is needed and what goes wrong without it, never lowered because capture is hard; readiness: 1 only in someone's head, 3 scattered files or a manual export, 5 written down and current in a tool the client uses) and each quadrant (high is 4 or 5: populate_now high value and high readiness, capture_first high value with readiness 3 or less, fill_in value 3 or less with high readiness, defer both 3 or less, unscored when either score is Unknown). first_build is one area from areas: the highest-value populate_now area whenever one exists, else the highest-value capture_first area, else the area the client most needs. test_question is a question the source says customers or the team ask, in its words. A tool that offers a connector is not a connection: never say a source is connected, and check any connector claim on the vendor's official page before it reaches the deck. Exactly 4 plan steps, each naming one who: Owner or one role the source names, never another and never two roles joined by or; exactly 2 next steps. Delete any later item the source gives no need for. Keep IDs, quotes, evidence and numeric scores off the slides. Ask the user for the client's logo; never invent one. Render with the pinned branding and the knowledge base deck layout; verify asset hashes and inspect every slide. If an asset is unavailable, follow the fallback rule and disclose it. Claim only files actually created. Disclose corrections separately from the deck. STATIC HOST METADATA layout_instructions: Knowledge base assessment deck, laid out like the AI Opportunity Assessment report deck: 16:9 slides at 1920x1080, one landscape PDF page per slide, in the shared style on a full-bleed #000000 canvas (slides 5 and 7 on #1A1A1A). Keep each slide's order, fixed words, sizes and positions as given here; never restyle, rename or add slides. A slot without content is dropped, never padded or left blank. Safe area: padding 92px top, 120px left and right, 96px bottom; content starts 40px under the title. Header on slides 2-7: eyebrow in Montserrat 800 24px uppercase, letter spacing .22em, #F06000; the title 18px below in Montserrat 800 70px uppercase, line height 1.0, letter spacing .01em, #FFFFFF; no rule and no lead under it. Cards: #1A1A1A, 1px rule border, padding 34px 36px, square corners, no shadows. Body text Inter 400; labels mono uppercase #8090A0, letter spacing .14em, unless stated. Every slide, 46px from the bottom: the footer Prepared with the AI Opportunity Assessment by AI Operator Academy. in Inter 20px #8090A0 at left and the page number (01 / 07) in mono 24px #8090A0, letter spacing .08em, at right. (1) Cover: centred vertically, KNOWLEDGE BASE in #FFFFFF over ASSESSMENT in #F06000, Montserrat 800 132px uppercase, line height .9; 30px below, Prepared for and the client, or the business type when the client is Unknown (#FFFFFF, 600), in Inter 34px #F0E0D0. Pinned to the bottom of the safe area, a full-width row with a 1px rule top border and 30px top padding: three columns packed to the left, each only as wide as its text and 84px apart: keys Assessment Date (today, written out, such as November 12, 2026), Business Type and Primary Focus in mono 24px, values 10px below in Inter 27px #FFFFFF. The client's logo sits top right inside the safe area, 120px high on a #FFFFFF panel with 14px padding, only when the user attached it (ask once; never fetch, redraw or invent it). (2) Executive Summary, eyebrow Where we are · where we’re going: a 1.25fr and 1fr grid with 32px gaps filling the slide. Left: two stacked equal cards, The Pain and The Outcome, each a Montserrat 800 30px uppercase #F06000 heading (letter spacing .16em) 18px above Inter 27px/1.5 #F0E0D0 text, centred vertically. Each quadrant card (padding 30px 32px) has its name at top, its areas under the name and its note at bottom, the notes exactly: Populate Now (top left, a #F06000 card, name Montserrat 800 40px uppercase #000000, note Inter 600 24px #000000) High value, ready now — build these first.; Capture First (top right) High value, not written down yet — capture it first.; Fill-Ins (bottom left) Lower value, ready — add when time allows.; Defer (bottom right) Lower value, hard to reach — leave for now.; the other names in Montserrat 800 32px uppercase #8090A0 (letter spacing .04em) over 24px #8090A0 notes. Each area in its quadrant as a tag, 10px apart, in Inter 600 22px with padding 8px 14px: #000000 on rgba(0,0,0,.18) in Populate Now, #FFFFFF on #242424 elsewhere. Unscored areas go on one mono line under the grid, such as Not yet scored · Warranty terms. Drop this slide when no area is scored. (5) Your 4-Step Build Plan, eyebrow Build the first area, on #1A1A1A: four equal columns with 26px gaps filling the slide; each card #1A1A1A with a 1px rule border and padding 34px 32px: the number 1 to 4 in Montserrat 800 88px, line height .9, #F06000; Step One to Step Four 10px below in Montserrat 800 26px uppercase #FFFFFF (letter spacing .14em); the task 22px below in Inter 27px/1.45 #F0E0D0; at the bottom, over a 1px rule with 22px padding, one uppercase line: WHO · in mono 24px #8090A0 (letter spacing .1em) and, on the same line, who in Montserrat 800 uppercase #F06000. (6) What It Unlocks, eyebrow The next phase: three top-aligned columns 32px apart, no cards, the row centred vertically, one per later item (the remaining columns stay empty): the number 01 in Montserrat 800 96px, line height .85, #F06000; a 60x2px rule2 line with 26px above and below; text in Inter 500 42px/1.25 #FFFFFF; name 18px below in mono 24px (letter spacing .1em). Drop this slide without a later item. (7) Your Next Steps, eyebrow Let’s get moving, on #1A1A1A: the two steps centred vertically, 30px apart, at most 1320px wide: the number in Montserrat 800 80px #F06000 in a 96px column, 34px gap; heading in Montserrat 800 42px uppercase #FFFFFF (letter spacing .02em); detail 12px below in Inter 27px/1.45 #F0E0D0, at most 980px wide; 14px under step 2, the button Schedule Your Review Call → on #F06000 in Montserrat 800 28px uppercase #000000 (letter spacing .08em), padding 24px 40px. Number the slides in order (01 / 06 when one is dropped). Character limits are maxima, not targets; shorten copy rather than shrinking type or clipping. Use Montserrat, Inter and the authentic logo only after verifying the supplied asset hashes; never redraw, recolor or replace the logo. If the logo or a font cannot be fetched or verified, ask the user to attach the verified files; without them, return the reviewed content in chat, or, if the user accepts, use the fallback wordmark AI OPERATOR ACADEMY in Montserrat 800 uppercase #FFFFFF over a 72x3px #F06000 rule, disclosed in chat and never presented as the logo.
